t: No later than 4 months after the date of enactment of this Act, and no later than March 15 of each year thereafter, the Advisory Commission on Intergovernmental Relations shall submit to the Congress, including the Committee on Government Reform and Oversight of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Governmental Affairs of the Senate, and to the President a report describing any Federal court case to which a State, local, or tribal government was a party in the preceding calendar year that required such State, local, or tribal government to undertake responsibilities or activities, beyond those such government would otherwise have undertaken, to comply with Federal statutes and regulations.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that an advisory commission, which may include state and local members, is taking part in federal decisionmaking. But the section only requires a descriptive report to Congress and the President cataloguing past court cases. It is not tied to any pending federal decision and sets up no consultation, comment, hearing, or right to sue. This is a close call because the reporting body is an advisory commission, but a purely informational report to Congress stays on the "No" side of the definition.
fable.s: the Advisory Commission on Intergovernmental Relations shall submit to the Congress, including the Committee on Government Reform and Oversight of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Governmental Affairs of the Senate, and to the President a report

qwen_block.w: This section requires a commission to submit a report to Congress and the President. Both Congress and the President are inside the federal government. The definition explicitly states that reports to Congress or its committees are not participation. Although the report concerns state and local governments, the interaction described is a one-way report to federal officials, not a consultation or coordination with outside parties before a decision is made.
qwen_block.s: the Advisory Commission on Intergovernmental Relations shall submit to the Congress... and to the President a report

opus.w: This is a requirement to report to Congress and the President, who are inside the federal government, about past federal court cases. Outside parties play no part in any upcoming federal decision. The Commission's intergovernmental makeup and the mention of state, local and tribal governments may look like participation, but those governments are only the subject of the report, not participants in a decision.
opus.s: the Advisory Commission on Intergovernmental Relations shall submit to the Congress, including the Committee on Government Reform and Oversight of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Governmental Affairs of the Senate, and to the President a report describing any Federal court case
opus.b: **Step 1: Reasoning.** It is tempting to read this as participation because the Advisory Commission on Intergovernmental Relations includes state, local and public members, and the report is about state, local and tribal governments. That reading fails. The section only requires a report on past court cases, sent to Congress, its committees and the President, all of whom are inside the federal government. It sets up no consultation, comment period, hearing or advisory input from outsiders before any federal decision. Like Example 3, it concerns the contents of a report, not input into a decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section requires the Advisory Commission on Intergovernmental Relations to submit a report to Congress and the President. According to the definition, reports to Congress or the President are considered internal government actions because Congress and the President are inside the federal government. There is no requirement for the federal government to consult with or coordinate with outside parties (such as the general public, states, or tribes) before making a decision in this specific text; rather, it mandates a reporting obligation to federal entities.
qwen_chat.s: the Advisory Commission on Intergovernmental Relations shall submit to the Congress... and to the President a report
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the Advisory Commission on Intergovernmental Relations (ACIR) is an advisory body, its existence implies participation. However, the specific action described in this section is the submission of a report *to* Congress and the President. Congress and the President are inside the federal government. The definition explicitly states that reports to Congress are "No" because they stay inside the government. The ACIR itself is not consulting with outsiders in this specific clause; it is reporting its findings to insiders. Furthermore, the ACIR was a federal agency/commission, and its members were often appointed by federal officials, but even if they included outsiders, the *action* mandated here is a report to the federal government, not a consultation *by* the federal government with outsiders before a decision. The definition says: "reports to, or notifications of, Congress... are inside the federal government... Answer 'No'".
